title: Policy Autotuner + Safe Apply Playbook for Per-Customer/Per-Route Cost Controls
creator: Marina Ortiz
description: Build an automated policy autotuner and safe-apply playbook that produces per-customer and per-route batching/caching recommendations and applies them with staged safety gates. The autotuner should synthesize segmentation rules, allowlist/denylist expressions, and tier caps based on historical traffic fingerprints and budget targets. Key goals: (1) reduce per-token cost without violating latency SLOs, (2) provide auditable simulation and explainability for each recommendation, (3) support non-destructive shadow testing and deterministic rollback, and (4) expose actionable UI and API hooks for PMs and support engineers.
acceptance_criteria: Autotuner can generate candidate policies for at least three customer segments (high-throughput, bursty, low-volume) using a 30-day traffic sample.
Each candidate includes estimated cost delta, expected p50/p95 latency impact, and a confidence score computed from simulation runs.
Safe-apply pipeline executes a shadow test for 48 hours and produces a comparison report (baseline vs candidate) before any live canary.
Canary rollout supports staged percentages (1%, 5%, 20%) with automatic rollback triggers evaluated at each stage.
Policy changes are recorded in audit logs with before/after configs, triggers, operator, and a human-readable rationale.
UI surfaces recommendations and allows one-click approve/schedule/rollback with links to the simulation artifact and prom queries used for evaluation.
implementation_notes: Policy schema: support route selector expressions, tenant predicates, cost_budget, latency_slo_ms, prefetch_kv_ttl_ms, batch_window_ms, kv_cache_allowlist/denylist patterns, and tier_id.
Storage: persist policies in PolicyStore (Postgres table 'seg_policies' with immutable audit rows). Use JSONB for policy payload but maintain indexed columns for tenant_id, route_hash, and tier_id.

Autotuner algorithm: combine gradient-free search (bayesian bandit) over discrete knobs (batch_size, batch_timeout, kv_ttl) with simulation-based evaluation using a 30-day replay engine that respects token-level arrival patterns and model-sequencing characteristics.
Simulation engine: run deterministic replay in a sandbox runtime that can instrument cost per-op and emulate prefix caching behavior; produce per-route cost curves and latency percentiles.
Safety gates: shadow mode -> canary (%) -> ramp. Each stage evaluates rollback triggers and quality regressions against golden prompts sampled per-route.
Telemetry: emit policy.event (policy_id, stage, outcome, metrics_snapshot) and policy.simulation artifacts URL to observability pipeline.
Audit log schema (human-readable): 'actor, action, policy_id, before_sha, after_sha, rationale, simulation_url, timestamp'.
Backward compatibility: when policy targeting overlaps, use deterministic precedence (tenant > route > global) and surface overlaps in the UI for manual resolution.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Design review with PM and Security. Freeze schema and API contract.
Phase 1: Implement PolicyStore and simulation API. Add telemetry events and storage for simulation artifacts.
Phase 2: Build autotuner core and run offline experiments against 50 representative tenants. Validate cost and latency estimates within 10% of real run.
Phase 3: Internal shadow rollouts on non-production clusters for full 48-hour runs and QA sign-off.
Phase 4: Canary to 1% of traffic for 24 hours, evaluate rollback triggers, then ramp to 5% and 20% with automated checks. Manual approval required before >20%.
Phase 5: General availability and docs, add UI controls for schedule/disable and per-tenant opt-out.
monitoring_playbook: Dashboards: policy-cost-comparison (baseline vs active), per-tenant latency heatmap, canary-stage metrics.
Critical alerts: cost_delta_pct > 15% for any tenant OR p95_latency increase > 30ms for 10 minutes.
Secondary alerts: simulation_confidence < 0.6, missing golden prompt evaluations, failed telemetry emits.

Runbook steps: extract policy.event and simulation artifacts, revert to last known-good policy (immutable audit row), open incident PR with policy_id and simulation URL, notify customer success if customer-facing tier impacted.
rollback_triggers: Cost increase for targeted tenant > 12% over baseline for two consecutive evaluation windows (10m each)
Error rate (5xx) increase > 0.5% absolute or >100% relative compared to baseline across affected routes
Latency p95 breach beyond configured latency_slo_ms for 5 minutes
Quality regressions detected on golden prompt set (BLEU/ROUGE/embed-sim drop beyond threshold) during canary
Manual abort by on-call or owner with documented rationale
review_comments: PM (Aditi Rao): Please ensure the UI shows confidence and a short natural-language rationale for each recommendation.
Security (Jonas Meyer): KMS access for simulation artifacts is required; ensure artifacts stored in encrypted bucket with least-privilege ACLs.
Design (Sofia Park): Add visual flagging for overlapping policies and an explicit preview mode in the console.
Eng (Rahul Patel): Need to limit autotuner compute budget (max 2h per tenant) and queue jobs to avoid interference with production autoscaling.
